title: Localization of graded cohomology at a section
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let L be an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let s be a global section of L, and let F be a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Assume X is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For n >= 0 let L^{tensor n} be the tensor power and X_s the open subscheme of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; for n < 0 put L^{tensor n} = (L^vee)^{tensor (-n)}, with L^vee the dual of [def-sc-invertible-module]. For p >= 0, set H_*^p(X,L,F) = direct sum over n in Z of H^p(X,F tensor L^{tensor n}) [pqf-def-cohomology], with its graded module structure over the graded ring Gamma_*(X,L) = direct sum over n >= 0 of Gamma(X,L^{tensor n}) induced by tensor product and multiplication of sections. Let H_*^p(X,L,F)_{(s)} be the degree-zero part of the localization of H_*^p(X,L,F) at the homogeneous element s of degree 1, i.e. the module of fractions xi/s^n with n >= 0 and xi homogeneous of degree n. Then the canonical map H_*^p(X,L,F)_{(s)} to H^p(X_s,F restricted to X_s), sending xi/s^n to s^{-n} xi (restrict xi to X_s, where s^n is a trivializing section of L^{tensor n}, and divide by it), is an isomorphism.
